fields.description: Replace per-job workflow, attempt and event writes with bounded batch statements in the existing claim transaction. Preserve audit rows, workflow status guards, lease/resource fencing, claim origins and rollback. Add live regressions and run the repository verification script. Prioritize implementation; follow with a focused statement-count and RTT comparison.
fields.title: Batch job-claim audit and workflow writes

data.text: Implemented three batch side-effect statements in the existing claim transaction: one guarded workflow update and two INSERT SELECT writes from the already locked queue rows. Candidate/resource acquisition, leasing and commit error handling are unchanged. No public API or schema change; ADR-010 review finds no new consumer-controlled state transition or coordination obligation. Regenerated the three checked-query metadata entries with the repository SQLx 0.9.0 refresh tool against disposable PostgreSQL 18.6 and retained unrelated cache entries. Focused claim_batch_writes suite passed all 3 tests: four claim variants, 16/single/empty statement counts, audit identity and metadata, resource fences, workflow status/first-start guards and full rollback after each injected batch failure. Full scripts/verify.sh now running on pinned Rust 1.98.1.

Focused post-implementation measurement completed on Linux x86_64 / PostgreSQL 18.6. A temporary psycopg 3.3.6 probe executed old SQL from HEAD checked-query metadata and new SQL from generated metadata over a TCP delay proxy. Fixture: 16 claimed jobs, 8 workflow-linked; three warmup pairs then 12 alternating samples per version; timed only side effects, after leasing and before rollback. pg_stat_statements observed 48 versus 3 statements and exactly 40 row writes in both (8 workflow + 16 attempts + 16 events). Added RTT 0/2/5 ms gave calibrated SELECT 1 medians 0.31/2.60/5.41 ms and old/new medians 20.53/4.34, 132.06/16.51, 294.97/36.20 ms. This is a bounded SQL-phase probe, not end-to-end worker throughput or SQLx-driver evidence. Command: uv run --no-project --with psycopg[binary] python /tmp/batter-claim-mn9t/measure.py; local raw results /tmp/batter-claim-mn9t/measurement.json. Durable statement-count regression also observes the actual Rust public claim paths. No repository dependencies or migrations changed.

Final verification PASSED: bash scripts/verify.sh exited 0 on pinned Rust 1.98.1, Linux x86_64. It ran formatting, file budgets, all four Clippy configurations, all six matrix parts (workspace, no-default-features, doctests, consumers, runlimit, scripts), rustdoc and all five HTTP smoke profiles. Workspace test part passed in 428.681 seconds; copied-source Runledger and single-facade consumer checks also passed. Focused claim_batch_writes tests passed all 3 cases before the full run. Final git diff --check passed; Cargo.lock, migrations and public signatures remain unchanged, and canonical/postgres/runtime SQLx metadata agree. No semantic tests were relaxed, no local MSRV run, and no code commit or publication performed. Full verification log is /tmp/batter-claim-mn9t/verify.log; focused log is /tmp/batter-claim-mn9t/claim-tests.log. The disposable metadata/measurement PostgreSQL container was removed. Implementation, regression tests, native contract/changelog, status row, testing evidence and primary references are complete.

fields.description: Review PR 54 directly from claim transaction invariants and ownership boundaries. Execute positive controls and deliberate mechanism ablations against PostgreSQL without retaining mutations. Report reproducible findings, causal evidence and limitations; preserve the implementation unless a verified defect requires repair.

data.text:
Direct first-principles and adversarial review: PR 54
Reviewed commit: e453a379b26180992d7c82ab81ac7c867bfad73c
Date: 2026-10-14
Environment: Linux x86_64, Rust 1.98.1, PostgreSQL 18.6, SQLx 0.9.0.

Conclusion: no confirmed correctness defect in the batched claim implementation.
Keep the current design. Physical audit rows remain proportional to the number
of claims, but sequential side-effect statements are constant at three for a
nonempty batch. Atomicity comes from the existing transaction, independently
of batching. The public claim APIs and persisted contracts are unchanged.

The candidate query takes FOR UPDATE locks before leasing; those locks remain
through both INSERT SELECT operations and commit. Queue rows supply run, attempt
and stage directly. One UUID list selects the returned claimed rows, avoiding
paired metadata arrays. Candidate resource acquisition and later lease-identity
fences remain unchanged. A unique workflow_steps.job_id keeps the linkage one
step per job; cancellation takes job locks before workflow locks. Workflow
transitions retain the ENQUEUED/RUNNING predicate, first start and output reset.
The queue helper owns audit writes and the existing workflow helper owns its
transition. Combining all writes into a larger SQL expression would add
coordination complexity without being needed for the requested batching.

Executed controls and ablations against the same three integration tests:
- Unchanged control: 3/3 passed before and after all mutations. These tests cover
  all four claim APIs, mixed direct/workflow jobs, both origins, varied identities,
  resource ownership, 16/1/0-job claims, and failures after each batch statement.
- Restore original per-job implementation: only statement-count test fails;
  16 statements per side-effect table (48 total), expected one each (3 total).
  Workflow preservation and rollback still pass.
- Remove workflow status fence: guarded-row snapshot fails.
- Remove workflow claimed-ID fence: unclaimed ninth step becomes RUNNING.
- Suppress attempt rows: per-job audit comparison finds no attempt.
- Suppress LEASED event rows: per-job audit comparison finds no lease event.
- Replace attempt identity with 1: audit records attempt 1 instead of claimed 2.
- Commit leasing before side effects: fault snapshot finds retained leases and
  resource claims. Timestamp assertions also fail.
- Reset first started_at: preserved-field count is 2 instead of 4.
- Retain old workflow output: cleared-output count is 0 instead of 4.
- Remove audit claimed-ID fences: 17 attempts/events appear instead of 16.

All ten mutations compiled and failed the intended behavioral assertions.
Compiler failures were not counted as detected regressions. Tests were not
edited. Each mutation was restored immediately; the final worktree is clean.
SQLx checked changed SQL against the disposable database (SQLX_OFFLINE=false),
without editing committed caches, migrations or Cargo.lock.

Additional tests with the restored code and committed offline metadata:
- job_execution_resources: 12/12 passed, including 100 competing claimers,
  mixed batches and filtered claimers contending for resources in opposite order.
- queue_lease_validation: 3/3 passed, including ordered writes and event failure.
- workflow_cancel_lock_order: 17/17 passed, including cancellation, continuation,
  completion, and dependent-release races.

Scope: this is direct code review and executed fault testing, not an independent
multi-model review. Ten selected mutations establish sensitivity to those faults,
not exhaustive proof over arbitrary interleavings or administrator schema changes.
No production workload or real network benchmark was added during this review.
The previously passed full verification run remains applicable to the unchanged
commit. GitHub reports all seven PR checks successful for this same commit.

Artifacts: run.py, results.json, each numbered .patch/.log, restoration.json,
neighbor-results.json and the two neighbor suite logs in this directory.
Primary locking reference rechecked:
https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/explicit-locking.html#LOCKING-ROWS
INSERT reference:
https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/sql-insert.html

data.reason: Completed direct adversarial review of PR 54: no confirmed defects; 10/10 compiled ablations detected, both control runs and 32 contention/lease/cancellation tests passed. Mutations restored, worktree clean, owned PostgreSQL container removed; detailed evidence recorded in issue comment.
